ours.what: ggml-org/llama.cpp a7b94df (our pinned build, native on the Pi 08:51)

ours-repack.what: ggml-org/llama.cpp a7b94df, SAME binary as 'ours' but WITHOUT -nr (llama.cpp's default weight repacking: eligible tensors are copied into anonymous CPU_REPACK memory; different memory layout, resident-only reference)

purpose: TUNING pass 2 (2 tuning requests only), declared 2026-10-05 23:05 after pass 1 and before any held-out request. (a) Re-runs the two pass-1 blocks that never started (both servers failed to re-bind port 18090 inside the 60 s TIME_WAIT; the driver now uses one port per block). (b) POST-HOC ADDITION to the grid: 'ours-repack' = our a7b94df binary without -nr. Reason: pass 1 showed a 2.8x prefill gap, and -nr is known to slow llama.cpp's kernels (E0, x86: prefill 0.66x), so comparing ik only against our -nr build could overstate ik. ik's analogous option -rtr is NOT run: it disables mmap and would hold ~12.1 GiB of weights in anonymous memory, leaving MemAvailable ~2.2 GiB < the 3 GiB safety floor on this board. (c) REVISED RULE (the pass-1 rule 'smallest sum of total latency' is confounded by reply length: ik produced 41 vs 59-63 tokens for tun-01 depending on the config): per engine choose the config with the smallest S = sum over the 2 tuning requests of [TTFT + (n_predict - 1) / client decode rate], i.e. the projected time to prefill and to generate the full bound; ties within 2 % go to -t 4, then (ik) to --swa-compress.
